name: India state boundaries (Survey of India based) and Census 2011 district boundaries
source_org: DataMeet India community (from Survey of India and Census of India maps)
limitations: Community digitisation of official maps. The outline follows India's official position, including areas administered by Pakistan and China.
method: Polygons projected to the grid; ~73 sample points per hex give area shares (pipeline/grid.py).

name: India district boundaries (~2020 vintage, 724 districts)
source_org: udit-001/india-maps-data (derived from DataMeet / LGD-era district maps)
limitations: Districts created after ~2020 (for example the 2022 Andhra Pradesh reorganisation) are not separate. Delhi is one polygon. Licence is not stated.
method: 34 state-outline features without a district name are removed. Same sampling as above.

name: Areas inside India's official outline administered by Pakistan or China
source_org: DataMeet (from US Department of State LSIB and other public sources)
limitations: Used only to mark hexes as 'claimed by India, administered by Pakistan/China'. All statistics are missing in these hexes.
method: A hex is marked when at least half of its sample points fall in these polygons.

name: Natural Earth 1:10m admin-0 (India point of view), rivers (scale rank), lakes
limitations: Generalised at 1:10 million. Rivers include only the main channels.
method: Neighbour countries and lakes sampled on the grid; rivers simplified (0.02°) and projected.

name: AWS Terrain Tiles (Terrarium encoding), zoom 7
source_org: Mapzen / Amazon Open Data (SRTM, GMTED2010, ETOPO1 and others)
license: Various open licences; attribution required (see landing page)
method: Mean, standard deviation and maximum of the hex sample points; used for relief classes and ocean/coast.

name: MODIS Combined Land Cover (MCD12Q1) IGBP classification, 2023
source_org: NASA LP DAAC, via NASA GIBS
limitations: Satellite classification. 'Forest' here is a land-cover class and differs from the Forest Survey of India forest-cover definition.
method: Class share among the hex sample points; dominant group gives the terrain cover (pipeline/world.py).

name: Gridded Population of the World v4, population density 2020
source_org: NASA SEDAC (CIESIN, Columbia University), via NASA GIBS
limitations: Modelled from census inputs. The GIBS colour map is binned and its top bin is ≥ 1,000 people/km², so values are capped at 1,000.
method: Each pixel colour is decoded to the middle of its colour-map bin, then averaged over the hex.

name: VIIRS Black Marble night lights, 2016 composite
limitations: A visual RGB composite, not calibrated radiance. Values are relative brightness 0–255.
method: Luminance (0.2126 R + 0.7152 G + 0.0722 B) averaged over the hex.

name: Global Natural Disaster Hotspots: flood, drought, cyclone frequency and landslide hazard
source_org: NASA SEDAC (CIESIN / World Bank / UNEP / NGI), via NASA GIBS
limitations: Old observation periods (1980–2003). Use only for broad patterns.
method: Colour decoded to the class value; open top classes take their lower bound; averaged over the hex.

name: WorldClim 2.1 climate normals 1970–2000 (10 arc-minute)
license: Free for non-commercial and research use (see landing page)
limitations: Interpolated station climatology. Not recent years.
method: Monthly precipitation summed; monthly mean temperatures averaged; hottest/coldest month; June–September rain share.
